title: Argument
normalizedStatement: An argument is a sequence of statements, the last of which is called the conclusion and the rest of which are called premises . An argument is said to be valid provided the conclusion must be true whenever the premises are all true. An argument is invalid if it is not valid; that is, all the premises can be true, and the conclusion could still be false. An argument is sound provided it is valid and all the premises are true. A proof of a statement is a sound argument whose conclusion is the statement.

title: Mini Sudoku Definitions
